gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the signal from the sound booth to a ceiling projector has to travel over an HDBaseT pair. AV Access's 4KEX70-H2 kit carries a WUXGA projector's native 1920×1200@60 up to 60 m over Cat5e/6 or 70 m over Cat6a, and one power adapter at the booth end powers both units. AV Access says its transmitter works only when connected directly to its own receiver, so the receiver must go into the projector's HDMI input and must not be skipped by plugging the transmitter into the projector's built-in HDBaseT port.
standout_why: I compared four rival pages. projectorcentral.com (Top 10 church projectors, 2026-11-08) mentions long cable runs only for 3G-SDI on $22k–$50k Epson Pro models. It says nothing about HDMI length, HDBaseT or extenders. itechguides.com (2026-10-12) says only that 'A long run may need an appropriate transport method' and lists 'HDBaseT listed' in a spec table without explaining it. projectorverdict.com covers re-running HDMI across the platform and M4-vs-VESA mount holes, but gives no distances and no extender advice. projectorsourcing.com would not load because of a certificate error, so I did not compare it. Neither ChatGPT answer covers getting the signal to the projector. They have pieces of the topic but nothing with distances, resolutions, power placement or pairing rules, which is why I scored this 2, not 3.
kit_items: Projector: Epson PowerLite L690U (6,500 lm, WUXGA laser), ChatGPT's pick for a medium sanctuary. It has HDBaseT plus HDMI, but the kit below feeds its HDMI input, so the HDBaseT port's compatibility with other brands doesn't matter.

Signal link: AV Access 4KEX70-H2 HDBaseT transmitter and receiver kit, sold only as a pair. Its spec table lists 1920×1200@60. It reaches 60 m on Cat5e/6 and 70 m on Cat6a at 1080p-class resolution, but only 35–40 m at 4K. One 18 V adapter at either end powers both units.

Cable: a straight-through Cat6a run with T568B ends on both sides, connecting the transmitter and receiver directly with no Ethernet switch in between. AV Access says patch cords at each end should be no longer than 5 m. Epson's minimum for HDBaseT is Cat5e STP.

items: AV Access 4KEX70-H2 4K HDBaseT Extender HDMI 2.0 up to 70m (TX+RX kit) | https://www.avaccess.com/products/4KEX70-H2/ | $156.72 (marked down from $164.99) | 2026-11-10

findings.note: It won't work through the church's network switch, and the page makes no claim that it works with third-party HDBaseT displays or projectors. That's the trap: plugging the transmitter straight into the projector's HDBaseT port is unsupported.

findings.source_title: PowerLite L690U 6,500-Lumen WUXGA 3LCD Laser Projector | Epson US

findings.label: Epson's HDBaseT cable rule and side effects
findings.value: Cat5e STP or better, up to 100 m (328 ft); turning on Control Communications disables the projector's LAN and RS-232C ports; Extron XTP sources need a separate menu setting; power both devices off before connecting or disconnecting the cable
findings.source_title: Connecting to an HDBaseT Transmitter (Epson user's guide, EB-L520U/L735U family per file paths)
findings.note: This page is from the guide for a sibling model, not the L690U. The same wording appears on the L510U/L610U guide (cpd55504, read 2026-11-10). The EB-L890E guide (cpd65465) adds 'operation is not guaranteed for all input/output devices and environments.'
